title: One million hearts added to the Knowledge Portals
summary: The Knowledge Portals now include genetic associations, polygenic risk score files, credible sets, and gene prioritization for coronary artery disease from a just-published CARDIoGRAMplusC4D study of over a million subjects.
bodyHtml:
We are pleased to announce that the Knowledge Portals now include the largest-to-date study of the genetics of coronary artery disease, shared here with the worldwide cardiometabolic disease ressearch community by the CARDIoGRAMplusC4D consortium. The study, published today in Nature Genetics (Aragam, Jiang, Goel, et al., 2022), is a GWAS for coronary artery disease (CAD) in more than 200,000 CAD cases and one million controls, discovering 82 novel associations. The authors also performed fine-mapping, generated a genome-wide polygenic risk score that predicts both incident and recurrent CAD, and used multiple lines of evidence to predict 220 candidate CAD causal genes. This "explainer" video from Jeanette Erdmann summarizes the study.

You can explore the results from this paper in the Knowledge Portals in multiple ways.

  • The CAD GWAS results are integrated into the Portals in four datasets:
    • CARDIoGRAMplusC4D 2022 CAD GWAS: trans-ancestry
    • CARDIoGRAMplusC4D 2022 CAD GWAS: females, trans-ancestry
    • CARDIoGRAMplusC4D 2022 CAD GWAS: males, trans-ancestry
    • CARDIoGRAMplusC4D 2022 CAD GWAS: European ancestry
  • The CAD credible sets may be viewed in the Variant Sifter tool.
  • The candidate CAD causal gene prioritizations are available from the Predicted Effector Genes landing page under the upper Tools menu.
  • GWAS summary statistics, credible sets, and PRS files are available for download from the Downloads page of the Cardiovascular Disease Knowledge Portal and the Downloads page of the Common Metabolic Diseases Knowledge Portal. The effector gene predictions and supporting evidence are available for download from the predicted CAD effector genes interface.
